description: endswith tests a suffix exactly as endsWith does, so file names sort into kinds
startswith tests a prefix exactly as startsWith does, and the match is case-sensitive
A string joins a list with itself as the separator, exactly as the list's join with that separator
join takes a class population, so a string can join the names of every instance
code:
class Tag(name):
    this.name = name
Tag("red")
Tag("blue")
" | ".join(Tag.map(tag -> tag.name))

description: A standing join with the separator as the receiver follows later pushes to its list
A separator held in a variable keeps the join live when the separator changes
code:
parts = ["2026", "11", "16"]
sep = "-"
day = sep.join(parts)
sep = "/"
day

description: A class-level rule with endswith follows each instance's own name
code:
class File(name):
    this.name = name
$File.table = $File.name.endswith(".csv")
notes = File("notes.txt")
notes.name = "notes.csv"
notes.table

description: Like startsWith, startswith ignores a position argument, unlike Python
join writes items that are not strings in their string form, where Python raises
A string argument to join keeps raising the accepted TypeError; join does not iterate characters
code:
result = ""
try:
    result = "-".join("abc")
catch error:
    result = error
result

description: A failed update through an alias rolls back, so the rule keeps its value
code:
class File(name):
    this.name = name
$File.table = $File.name.endswith(".csv")
report = File("report.csv")
failure = ""
try:
    report.name = 7
catch error:
    failure = error
[report.name, report.table, failure]
